messages:
aisha: quick q — i pushed a small config change to infra-deploy that flips experimental batching off by default. do we need to bump the public version or tag this at all?
miguel: if it's strictly infra config and doesn't change any client-facing behavior, i'd prefer no semver bump. just note in the infra changelog.
sam: +1 on no bump, but if the change can alter latency or throughput for customers we should treat it as a behavior change and bump patch. this one could affect p95 under spike.
nina: depends on scope — is this behind a feature flag? can be rolled back without a tag?
aisha: flag is server-side, rollback is a fast flip. no code changes. the only risk is short-lived increased latency while cache warms.
sam: then i'd say: no public release number bump, but create a deployment tag for ops traceability. something like `v1.28.4+ops.1` or `ops/1.28.4-infra1` so we can map telemetry to the deploy.
miguel: personally i'd rather keep canonical tags as plain semver (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) and use lightweight metadata labels for infra-rolls. mixing buildmeta into semver confuses release consumers.
nina: can we standardize this? my vote: canonical tag `vX.Y.Z` only for application code changes that touch APIs. infra-only changes get `ops/<short-hash>-YYYYMMDD` and an entry in CHANGELOG-infra.md.
sam: rollback criteria: let's call out thresholds here so oncall knows when to revert: >1% 5xx over baseline sustained for 3m, p95 increase >200ms sustained 5m, or spike in error-rate for any customer of >0.5% requests. if any of these, rollback to previous infra config.
aisha: sounds good. also add an alert for opcode:infra-batch-warmup to surface transient latencies.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for infra-deploy on prod (canary=5%), commit=ab3f2d, user=aisha. watching windows: 15m.
miguel: tagging convention follow-up: we should add a short section in release-playbook explaining "what counts as a semver bump" and provide examples (config flip, telemetry-only, client API change). i'll draft it.
nina: +1 — include guidance on release notes: infra-only => short entry under infra heading, no public release notes unless customer-visible impact.
sam: also call out backport policy: if we later decide it should've been a patch bump, we must create a true patch release with the same codebase and a clear release note explaining difference.
aisha: thanks — i'll proceed with the ops tag and monitor. miguel, please add the playbook blurb and i'll link it from the deploy checklist.
miguel: will do.
nina: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary passed (15m). promoting to 25% now.
deploy-bot: promoted to 100%. deployment complete.
sam: record kept in internal release tracker: infra-change ab3f2d -> ops/20231105-ab3f2d. no semver bump.
aisha: closing thread, thanks all :heart:
